liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Reviewer says this was the first Bird Song in seven years; Reviewer suggests this may have been the first acoustic set of 1980, opening with Bird Song [9][16]
- **Ripple** (2 reviews): Reviewer says this was the first Ripple in nine years; Reviewer describes this Ripple as strong and mellow [9][15]
- **I've Been All Around This World** (2 reviews): Reviewer says it was the first All Around This World in ten years; Reviewer found the performance sweet and was hearing the song for the first time [12][15]
- **Monkey And The Engineer** (1 review): Reviewer says this was the first Monkey and the Engineer in ten years [9]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Reviewer points out that this song was played acoustically [12]
- After technical glitches, Weir thanks the audience for tolerating the technical trouble before this song [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd80-09-25 s1t01 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t02 I've Been All Around This World**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t03 Dark Hollow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t04 Rosalie McFall**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t05 Monkey & The Engineer**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t06 It Must Have Been The Roses**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t07 Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **gd80-09-25 s1t08 Oh Babe It Ain't No Lie**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-09-25.144697.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 31 songs; 194 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd80-09-25.menke.vernon.7303.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 30 songs; 183 min; rated 3/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds hollow, with frequent crowd noise, and is weaker than a soundboard [11]
- **gd80-09-25.acoustic-sbd.hinko.18740.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 45 min; rated 4.54/5 by 13 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears static over Jerry's vocals on the soundboard; Reviewer finds the soundboard recording very clear; Reviewer finds the soundboard clean and crisp [13][14][15]
- **gd1980-09-25.144696.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 31 songs; 194 min [2]

## Around the show

- The audience is described as ecstatic, taking in every note [14]
- Answering shrieking audience members, Jerry says they figured they might as well try the acoustic format [16]
- Reviewer, who attended several shows in the run, rates the acoustic set on the 11th as the best [5]
- Reviewer recommends the soundboards of the Warfield run and the Radio City Music Hall shows that followed [11]
- Reviewer says this month's shows had the first acoustic sets in many years [12]
- Reviewer calls this the start of one of the most remarkable runs of shows in rock history [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-09-25.144697.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; (3) x Nakamichi 700 mics (left/right cardioids, omni center - handheld shoulder high)> Custom mixer by Jamie Poris >… [1]. Also: Master cassettes came from Mark Severson, transferred by Charlie Miller, who coordinated the effort; pitch correction was applied; Darryl Hinko's soundboard supplies the first 4:18 of Bird Song; the tape flip after Drums is cross-faded [1]
- **gd80-09-25.menke.vernon.7303.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak CM700's [3]. Also: Taped with three Nakamichi CM700 mics through a mixer into a Sony D-5, circulated via Douglas Ferguson and Matt Vernon [3]
- **gd80-09-25.acoustic-sbd.hinko.18740.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1980-09-25.144696.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; (3) x Nakamichi 700 mics (left/right cardioids, omni center - handheld shoulder high)> Custom mixer by Jamie Poris >… [2]
